grh_7baf6f6dcbb54979e383.title: The Living Doll
paragraphs: Cynthia Browning's lifelike doll, made with her own hair and nail clippings, is found stabbed through the heart, and Holmes learns that an old 'wise woman' has been hired to use black magic against the child. When the woman is found beaten to death, money around her seems to point toward suitors named King or Pound, but her final act is to clutch a sixpence. Remembering the slang term 'tanner' for that coin, Holmes exposes Hugh Tanner, who wanted Cynthia removed so Mrs. Browning would be free to marry him and then killed the ineffective accomplice to silence her. Tanner confesses before the police arrive.

[[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Basil Rathbone and Nigel Bruce. Other credited names include Edna Best as producer, Anthony Boucher as writer, Denis Green as writer, and Harry Bartell as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.bbd501bf461d302b|Petri Wines]] and [[org|org.bbd501bf461d302b|Petri Wines]].
This version is based on [[work|work.doyle.7b6fb1e44634fb61|The Adventure of the Copper Beeches]]. Arthur Conan Doyle is credited as author.

grh_7bafc96d94fa20d87d83.title: The Attic Stairway Murder Mystery
paragraphs: When wealthy Mrs. Parker is found dead at the bottom of her attic stairs, suspicion falls on her disabled housekeeper and former friend Mary Bignall, especially after Mrs. Parkers rings disappear. Dr. Christian learns that decades earlier Mrs. Parker had intercepted and switched letters between Mary and Ed Parker, then married Ed after an accident left Mary crippled. On the day of the death Mary finally found Eds original Valentine proving he had never rejected her; during their confrontation Mrs. Parker lost her balance and fell. Mary arranged the body and took the rings Ed had once meant for her, but Dr. Christian chooses to let the accidental death and Marys long suffering remain private.

grh_7b141b5a312af668dea0.title: The Arithmetic of Honor
paragraphs: East German escapee Hans returns to East Berlin a year after reaching the West, accompanied by a young West German woman who trusts and loves him. His real purpose is to steal her identity card and give it to another woman in East Berlin whom he has long promised to rescue. The deception succeeds in getting his intended companion safely across the border, but the innocent woman he used is left behind without papers and is arrested for possessing an identity that authorities now treat as stolen. Hans gains the freedom he promised one person by sacrificing another person's freedom and trust.
